chung.Syllabus Name: Basic typography & Layout _ Đồ họa chữ và bố cục cơ bản
chung.Description:
This course will cover the history, theory and practice of letterforms and

typography as they apply to graphics, advertising and other areas of design and

visual communication. Projects cover typography history, principles of

typography, letter structure, typeface selection, fundamentals of computer

typesetting.
chung.StudentTasks:
Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (www.cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

- Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submit to the teacher 1 day after the course.

taiLieu: Thinking with Type: A Critical Guide for Designers, Writers, Editors, & Students
clo: Classify typographic styles by period, noting key traits and contexts.
Explain typeface anatomy and how proportions, stroke dynamics, and metrics/spacing affect legibility and readability.
Evaluate typographic approaches for a given goal and their impact on meaning and hierarchy.
Design brief-fit typographic solutions with appropriate pairing, hierarchy/grid/rhythm, and correct specs.
Use technology tools and AI tools effectively across the typography workflow with responsible disclosure and verification.
danhGia: Group PresentTypeface Research. Students work in groups. Apply typographic theory with research methods (including responsible AI) to study one selected typeface: trace its history and development, profile the designer/foundry, analyze anatomy and features, review applications, and compare with other related typefaces using clear criteria.

Work in Group (3-4 students/group)

The evaluation will consider the following criteria: Research dossier & context (20%). Anatomy & legibility analysis (20%), Applications & usage guidelines (20%), Comparative critique (20%), Slide design & presentation (storytelling + Q&A) (20%). Students deliver a slide presentation with full documentation of the research process (AI Use Log) and present a counter-argument in Q&A.
Participation all activities during class time

- Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments.
- Lecturer give marks on student's student's Class participation and preparation only after the Portfolio submission.

Dissect one base typeface: document its key anatomy and metrics, then design a new typeface with a concise brief (purpose/voice), a minimum glyph set (A–Z, a–z, 0–9, punctuation; Vietnamese demo encouraged), defined metrics & spacing, and a specimen (one-page showcase of a typeface).

Individual work. The evaluation will consider the following criteria: Brief & research plan(20%). System definition (20%), Core making / prototyping (30%), Integration & iteration(20%), Final presentation & documentation (10%). Students report on assignment progress within the specified time, present research and work plan.

Students apply the instructor-approved typeface (your Practice 1 font or an existing face) to design assigned artifacts. Build a coherent typographic system (scales, hierarchy, spacing, grid), test readability/accessibility across media, and justify choices.

Individual work. The evaluation will consider the following criteria: Brief & research plan(20%). System definition (20%), Core making / prototyping (30%), Integration & iteration(20%), Final presentation & documentation (10%). Students report on assignment progress within the specified time, present research and work plan.

Students create a typographic work grounded in meaningful content (poetry, excerpts, slogans, etc.), translating that meaning into a structured typographic composition/system with hierarchy, rhythm, and an expressive voice, while also demonstrating application and material experimentation.

Individual work. The evaluation will consider the following criteria: Brief & research plan(20%). System definition (20%), Core making / prototyping (30%), Integration & iteration(20%), Final presentation & documentation (10%). Students report on assignment progress within the specified time, present research and work plan.

Design a communication poster for an instructor-defined goal (event/brand/product/service) with a typography-first approach. Build a clear type hierarchy, grid, rhythm, and real-world readability; imagery is optional and supportive.

Individual work. The evaluation will consider the following criteria: Brief & research plan(20%). System definition (20%), Core making / prototyping (30%), Integration & iteration(20%), Final presentation & documentation (10%). Students report on assignment progress within the specified time, present research and work plan.
